note: Twenty-five pages at 595.3x841.9 pt, twenty-five measured regions and twenty-one exhibits: Figures 1-20 and Table 1. The four leftover regions are the right halves of the four two-panel figures, excluded as fragments of their partner. There is no page furniture: no stamp, no watermark, nothing excluded for background, only a zero-height header hairline above the live-text running head. Captions print below the figures at a fixed 15.33 pt (31.55 pt on the pairs, which adds the (a)/(b) label band) and above the table at 12.76 pt. Four captions are bare labels with no words. Only twelve numbered pointers exist in the whole paper, so ten exhibits are never cited by number. rules: Twenty-one exhibits, both number runs complete and closed: Figures 1 to 20 with no gap and one Table 1. But citation is the thinnest in the block after the previous paper's two pointers: TWELVE numbered pointers in the whole document, spread over eleven exhibits, so ten of the twenty-one are never cited by number at all - Figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11 and 18. [mention.count] is 0 on those ten rows and non-zero on the other eleven.

Caption side is a paper-level decision with no exception: all twenty figure captions print BELOW and the single table caption prints ABOVE. The figure gap is a fixed offset of 15.33-15.34 pt on sixteen of them - so fixed that the four two-panel figures' 31.55 pt is exactly that offset plus the 16.2 pt (a)/(b) label band, not a second style. [caption.position] is 'below' twenty times and 'above' once, but [caption.position] alone cannot tell a single-panel from a paired figure: the gap can, and only if two constants are allowed.

Four captions carry NO descriptive words: 'Figure 10:', 'Figure 15:', 'Figure 16:' and 'Figure 18:' print as bare labels ending in a colon, and the description lives in the (a)/(b) sub-labels 6.7-6.9 pt under the boxes, outside the measured regions. [caption.words] is 2 on those four rows. A caption test that demands a noun phrase, or three words, or a capitalised title, silently drops a fifth of this paper's exhibits.

Numbering is one form only - 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:' with an ASCII colon, twenty of twenty-one - and this paper also prints a running head ('Team # 2200289 Page N of 24') that runs one behind the physical page. Two lines that begin with a figure number are NOT captions: p15's 'Figure 9.' and p17's 'Figure 13.' are the wrapped tails of body sentences, and both sit 200-450 pt above the art they name. [mention.lead_sentence] for Figures 9 and 13 quotes the wrapped pair.

Every two-panel figure in this paper is DISTORTED and every single-panel one is not: the four pairs are drawn as 875x656 (1.334) or 2400x1159 (2.071) rasters into 212.6x141.7 pt (1.500) boxes, so their x and y dpi disagree (296x333, 527x338, 525x320, 813x589), while all sixteen single-panel rasters match their box aspect to three decimals. Pairing, not scaling policy, is what breaks the aspect here - the opposite of a paper where one global scaling rule bites. [geometry.panel_count] is 2 on exactly those four rows and 1 on the other sixteen.

The pair geometry is exact and mechanical: gutter 3.0 pt, identical panel widths of 212.6 pt, identical top y within each pair, and (a)/(b) sub-labels 6.7-6.9 pt below the boxes. So the two halves of a figure are separated by 3.0 pt of white while the caption sits 31.55 pt down, which means a clustering rule that groups boxes by proximity merges the panels and then has to decide which of the two the caption belongs to by x-overlap - neither panel contains the caption's centre. [geometry.panel_layout] reads '1x2' on the four pairs and '1' on everything else.

One drawing is reused across figures and one course is rendered twice. Figures 5 and 6 print the same cyclist-and-bicycle silhouette - identical helmet, torso, frame, saddle and rear-derailleur cluster - rotated a few degrees and carrying different force vectors, so the reuse is invisible unless the two crops are put side by side. The self-designed course appears as Figure 13's isometric loop (0-11 km on both axes, one 200 m summit) and again as the elevation panel of Figure 18, a flat distance-elevation chart reaching 200 m at about 15 km of a 40 km perimeter. Figure 2 is NOT a third rendering of it: its 1259x276 strip is a thresholded terrain silhouette with a twin-peak skyline and no route line at all, which is why it is the paper's only 'other'. [geometry.family] therefore separates Figure 13 (surface-or-3D, isometric) from Figure 18 (line, taken from its sensitivity panel) although both describe one hill.

Family does not follow the caption's words here: 'Power Distribution(course1)' is a line, 'AWC Distribution' is a line, but the wind-sensitivity figures with equally flat captions are SCATTER - twelve unjoined dots each. The split is 10 line, 5 flowchart-or-schematic, 3 scatter, 1 surface-or-3D, 1 other, 1 table-grid, and the family is decided from the pixels: marker-only art versus joined traces is invisible in the text layer, which holds nothing inside any of these bitmap boxes, so [geometry.family] had to come from the crops.

Table 1 is the paper's only table and it is booktabs with a catch: exactly three horizontal strokes (top 107.3, header 122.1, bottom 512.6), no vertical rule and no side box, and all three run from x 72.0 to x 612.6 - 17.3 pt past the right edge of a 595.3 pt page - so the rules are clipped by the sheet and the table reads wider than the paper. A rule-fitting detector that trusts the drawn rect measures a table whose right edge does not exist on the page. [table.rule_style] is booktabs, [table.rows] is 28 and [table.cols] is 3.

No page furniture beyond a header rule: 25 pages, 25 measured regions, and every one of them is an exhibit or a panel of one. There is no stamp, no watermark and no background block anywhere in the file: the only repeated mark is a zero-height hairline running x 72.0-523.3 at y 48.9 (y 98.8 on the cover), which encloses nothing, and the running head is live text at y 37 that never intrudes into a box. So this paper's exclusion list is four panel fragments and nothing else, where the previous four papers in the block each had twenty-five to thirty-two furniture regions. Absence of furniture is itself a finding, and a census that expects a stamp per page would read this file as a failure, while one that subtracts any repeated rule would read the header hairline as twenty-five of them. [place.solo_page] is false on every row and no row carries a background exclusion.

tables.note: A 540.6x405.3 pt vector table, the paper's only one: a header row (Symbol | Description | Unit) and twenty-seven definition rows from P to fn, so 28 rows in three columns. The grid is horizontal only - exactly three strokes, at y 107.3 (top), y 122.1 (header) and y 512.6 (bottom), with no vertical rule and no side box anywhere - so rule_style is booktabs with a single (not double) top and bottom rule. All three rules run x 72.0 to 612.6, i.e. 17.3 pt PAST the right edge of a 595.3 pt page, so every rule is clipped by the paper edge and the table reads wider than the sheet. Each row prints three text baselines at slightly different y (symbol, description 0.3 pt higher, unit), so a baseline count reads 81 lines for 27 rows; the row count comes from the symbol column alone.
